heading: From seed to useful fractions
brief: 1 oilseed seeds and ground mixture; arrow to 2 a simple water-filled separation vessel; two branching arrows from 2 to 3 two distinct collection jars, one creamy protein fraction and one pale oil fraction; arrow from 3 to 4 test samples and a comparison chart
steps: Begin with an oilseed mixture.
Use a water-based separation process.
Recover different fractions, including proteins and oleosomes.
Test the properties needed for a useful ingredient.
note: The branches are conceptual fractions, not a complete mass balance or a proprietary equipment design.

heading: From sample to a spectrum
brief: 1 small sample tube within a simple magnet housing; arrow to 2 the same sample receiving a short radio-frequency pulse represented by a short wavy line; arrow to 3 a decaying oscillating signal chart; arrow to 4 a spectrum with several peaks
steps: Place the sample in a magnetic field.
Apply a radio-frequency pulse.
Record the response as a signal over time.
Transform the signal into a spectrum to interpret.
note: The signal and peaks are illustrative, not measured data. NMR is an extension beyond the required course treatment.

heading: Two routes to a tested part
brief: 1 blueprint of a bracket; arrow branches to 2 two parallel routes: layers building a bracket and a cutting tool removing chips from a block; arrows converge at 3 finished bracket and calipers; arrow to 4 bracket supporting a test load
steps: Define the part and its requirements.
Compare adding material with removing material.
Measure the finished dimensions.
Check whether the part meets its intended load and use.
note: Printing and machining can also be combined. The bracket is a fictional teaching example, not an Exergy client part.

heading: Follow the material into different streams
brief: 1 tank of dark slurry; arrow to 2 generic separation block with mesh and simple liquid vessel; three arrows branch to 3 separate jars containing recovered water, nutrient-rich liquid, and solids; arrow to 4 sample-testing rack
steps: Start with manure containing water and other material.
Apply physical and chemical separation steps.
Collect different water, nutrient and solid streams.
Test the outputs against their intended uses.
note: Clear appearance does not prove drinking-water quality. Actual performance requires measurements.

heading: From inspection to an evidence-based decision
brief: 1 aircraft component on workbench; arrow to 2 inspection magnifier and measuring tool; arrow to 3 comparison of a measurement with limits on a document; arrow to 4 maintenance record and two diverging paths, one to component reuse and one to repair
steps: Identify the component and the applicable procedure.
Inspect and measure its condition.
Compare the evidence with approved limits.
Record the authorized maintenance decision.
note: This is a conceptual decision sequence, not an inspection procedure or permission to return a part to service.

heading: A batch needs a traceable history
brief: 1 numbered-looking but textless sample vials; arrow to 2 small closed bioprocess vessel; arrow to 3 purification column and collection vial; arrow to 4 analytical chart beside batch records
steps: Define the material and starting conditions.
Produce a batch under recorded conditions.
Separate and purify the material.
Check identity, quality and consistency against the requirements.
note: This generic sequence does not assert that every Northern RNA service occurs at one Calgary facility.

heading: Observe, intervene, then measure again
brief: 1 small flock of birds near a distant runway with binoculars; arrow to 2 robotic falcon-shaped aircraft in flight away from runway; arrow to 3 observer with binoculars and a tally sheet; arrow to 4 two small comparison charts; return arrow from 4 back to 1
steps: Record bird activity before intervention.
Use the bird-shaped drone as one part of site management.
Continue observations after the intervention.
Compare results and consider other explanations.
note: The arrows show an evaluation plan, not a guaranteed effect. The cited airport deployment is outside Calgary.

heading: A scan is evidence to interpret
brief: 1 tray of cylindrical rock core; arrow to 2 enclosed scanner box above core; arrow to 3 aligned photograph, multicolour measurement strip and line trace; arrow to 4 geologist comparing the strips with a core sample
steps: Keep track of the rock sample and its position.
Collect measurements with scanning instruments.
Align different measurements of the same core.
Compare patterns with geological observations and further tests.
note: No particular mineral, grade or resource estimate is established by this illustration.

heading: Scale changes the engineering problem
brief: 1 small laboratory vessel; arrow to 2 simple flow drawing with tanks and arrows; arrow to 3 larger transportable demonstration skid with pipes and controls; arrow to 4 test records; return arrow from 4 to 2
steps: Start with a process demonstrated at laboratory scale.
Plan flow, equipment and control needs.
Build a larger demonstration system.
Use testing to revise the design.
note: The generic skid illustrates the documented Katal scale-up case; it is not a drawing of the actual machine.

heading: The same load over a different area
brief: 1 heavy load block with a downward weight arrow; arrow to 2 two identical loaded vehicle silhouettes, one with narrow wheels and one with wide tracks; arrow to 3 ground-contact footprints with small versus large shaded areas; arrow to 4 two patches of soft ground with deeper and shallower impressions
steps: A loaded vehicle pushes down on the ground.
Wheels and tracks create different contact areas.
The same force spread over more area gives lower average pressure.
Ground strength, traction and loading still affect whether it sinks.
note: A simplified equal-load comparison. This is not a prediction for a specific vehicle or soil.

heading: Track carbon through a process
brief: 1 two secured gas cylinders connected by pipes; arrow to 2 simple enclosed reactor with a small heat icon; arrow to 3 a sealed vial of dark solid carbon material; arrow to 4 material test coupons and a measurement chart
steps: Supply carbon-containing gases to the process.
Use controlled reaction conditions.
Recover solid carbon material.
Measure its properties and the process inputs and outputs.
note: This is not a balanced reaction diagram. Energy use and other streams matter when evaluating environmental claims.

heading: Capture, release and repeat
brief: 1 mixed-liquid jar with different colour dots; arrow to 2 column containing a porous solid with selected orange dots attached; arrow to 3 collected liquid with orange dots released from solid; arrow to 4 comparison chart of repeated cycles; clear return arrow from 3 back to 2 showing reuse
steps: Begin with a mixture containing lithium and other substances.
A selective material captures some lithium.
Release lithium into another stream and prepare the material for reuse.
Compare recovery and performance over repeated cycles.
note: Dots are conceptual, not literal ions or a disclosed sorbent structure. Commercial field activity is not assumed to occur in Calgary.

heading: Check a model against the site
brief: 1 generic industrial tank and survey tripod; arrow to 2 dotted point-cloud tank; arrow to 3 aligned wireframe and point-cloud tank with one visible gap; arrow to 4 tablet comparing model against real tank; return arrow from 4 to 1
steps: Collect spatial observations of a site.
Organize measurements into a digital representation.
Check alignment, missing areas and observation dates.
Compare with current conditions before using the model for a decision.
note: Detail is not the same as accuracy. The scene is generic, not a VEERUM customer installation.

heading: Move energy across time
brief: 1 sun and solar panel; arrow to 2 closed battery cabinet; arrow to 3 moon beside house with light on; arrow to 4 two small load symbols, a single lamp and several appliances with different timer icons
steps: Electricity is available at one time.
Store some energy for later use.
Discharge it when electricity is needed.
A larger load uses the stored energy faster.
note: The arrows show energy transfer, not creation. Losses, capacity and operating limits affect real runtime.

heading: From aircraft observations to weather information
brief: 1 passenger aircraft along a curved flight path through atmosphere; arrow to 2 small abstract sensor box and several plotted readings; arrow to 3 radio transmission to ground antenna; arrow to 4 weather map and vertical profile on screen
steps: Aircraft travel through different atmospheric conditions.
Sensors collect observations along the route.
Communication systems deliver data to the ground.
Meteorologists combine observations with other evidence and models.
note: Sensor capability depends on the installed system. Flight paths leave gaps; the map is illustrative, not a forecast.
